summary: The note describes art theft and looting during World War II on a massive scale. It states that the looting originated with the policies of the Axis powers, primarily Nazi Germany and Japan, which systematically looted occupied territories. It also notes that near the end of the war the Soviet Union began looting reclaimed and occupied territories, and that the scale of Nazi looting left many pieces scattered across the world.
one_line: Overview of large-scale art theft and looting during World War II by Axis powers and later the Soviet Union.
key_facts: Art theft and looting occurred on a massive scale during World War II.
The looting originated with the policies of the Axis countries, primarily Nazi Germany and Japan.
Nazi Germany and Japan systematically looted occupied territories.
Near the end of the war, the Soviet Union began looting reclaimed and occupied territories.
"The grand scale of looted artwork by the Nazis has resulted in the loss of many pieces being scattered across the world." (Minyard, 2007)
